reviewType: Independent AI close-reading and editorial review
reviewerIndependence: Reviewer extracted/collated the source and did not author this teaching part. A separate author supplied staggered drafts; recommendations were sent to the author and independently rechecked in the final file.
method: Read every English and Punjabi source-occurrence meaning alongside its exact immutable Gurmukhi.
Read all bilingual Salok/pauri studies, overviews, vocabulary, reflections, teach-back prompts and cautions.
Independently retrieved and read relevant Sahib Singh commentary sections on Ang292–296 for lexical/grammatical checks; modern commentary remains scratch-only.
Sent actionable findings to the author; re-read every adopted change in successive snapshots and the final authoring file.
Compared all final fields with the reviewed snapshot; mechanically verified the exact complete source groups, primary Ang links and source-file hashes.

lexicalAndContextualChecks.check: The image of a shared sustaining thread and equal regard governs the spiritual victory language.
Divine is retained as grammatical subject in the forgetting line; protection language is not used to diagnose another person’s suffering.
Service, Hukam, freedom from enmity and the hereafter are retained together.
The Divine is the subject of perfect understanding and fruitful vision; deathlessness retains the liberation frame.
The contextual Darpan reading of Sant as Guru is attributed; it is not asserted as a definition for every occurrence of Sant.
The all-within-One construction is read following the attributed commentary; deep absorption and unstruck sound retain their spiritual context.
Divine speech/presence is distinguished from an assertion that every human statement is truthful.
The realized person’s truthful speech, dharam and all-pervading vision remain explicit.
Sat affirms the reality/existence of creation, without making every temporary created form everlasting.
The Divine-body image and Maya’s obedience preserve the strong unity and agency language.
Divine goodness is retained, with ethical application explicitly connected to pauri4 rather than an incorrect preceding-pauri reference.
Living liberation, honor and the devotee’s liberating company are preserved; the final description is not mistranslated as an imperative.
Narak retains its explicit hell referent rather than becoming only a description of psychological distress.
Hearing and practising are linked; Saadh as Guru and mahant as elevated conduct are attributed contextual readings.
Household entanglement concerns attachment/vice rather than a command to abandon family care.
Sukhmani is linked to Divine virtues and Naam as the jewel of peace and spiritual steadiness.
The final two lines are linked grammatically: voicing and attentive hearing of Guru words/Naam; Nanak is vocative. Equal vision and the four traditional aims are explained.
Following the attributed Darpan reading, jug denotes lifetime, bani the devotee’s speech, matant the essence of teachings and karam Divine grace.
Roga retains disease/affliction, Saadh naam describes the person’s designation, karam means deeds, and the ending identifies Naam as Sukhmani.

refinementsVerified.change: Simplified English while preserving the Divine as grammatical subject.
Corrected Punjabi grammar to the one who knows essential reality.
Removed unintended untouchability/caste sense from the word used for invulnerability.
Smoothed Punjabi question about applying a teaching to an ordinary choice.
Corrected cross-reference to truthfulness and dharam in pauri4, not the preceding pauri6.
Changed ambiguous English imperative-like wording into a description of the liberated person bringing liberation to others.
Punjabi now explicitly says honored, avoiding ambiguity around pati.
Corrected Punjabi opening syntax linking vision to truthful conduct.
Explained the wisdom/vision metaphor directly, removing an unnecessary hypothetical eye-substance warning.
Confirmed and adopted the author’s more explicit reference to suffering of hell.
Both languages now express seeing everyone with equal impartial regard, consistent with the cited commentary.
Linked the closing pair clearly and made Nanak vocative in both languages, matching the stated interpretive construction.
Named and briefly explained the four traditional human aims.
Smoothed the Punjabi sentence about the wealth a person earns and carries.

limitations: This is AI editorial review, not qualified human Punjabi/Gurbani approval.
Interpretive checks follow selected attributed commentary; this is not a survey of every Sikh interpretive tradition.
Digital source agreement does not prove independent printed-edition lineage.
Review input is the named authoring JSON; integration adds metadata and approximate transliteration separately.
This teaching review makes no claim about browser behaviour or physical-device acceptance.
